question.problem: A child is playing with a tablet. The apps on the tablet are labeled with numbers $4$ through $21.$ If the child chooses an app at random, what is the probability that the app number they pick is more than $16?$
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the number of the app picked. From the problem statement, we know that $X∼U\{4,5,…,21\},$ and we wish to compute $P(X>16).$

In general, if $X$ follows a discrete uniform distribution over a set $S,$ then $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{|S|}, & x\in S \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have $X∼U\{4,5,…,21\},$ and the set $S=\{4,5,…,21\}$ has $|S|=21-4+1=18$ items. So, we have

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{18}, & x=4,5,…,21 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

In $S,$ the items that satisfy $X>16$ are $17,18,19,20,21.$ There are $5$ of these items. Therefore,

$$
P(X>16)=5\cdot \frac{1}{18}=\frac{5}{18}.
$$
